problem: Open-loop LLM planners produce static action sequences that fail in dynamic, partially observable real-world settings, and prior closed-loop systems mostly work only in simulation or depend on static task definitions (PDDL/BT/MCTS/TAMP).
motivation: Long-horizon embodied tasks need state tracking and online correction, but LLM context limits and unpredictable object states break static plans. The paper argues that decoupling observation, memory, planning and feasibility critique across open-source LLMs/VLMs enables closed-loop replanning on real robots.
key_idea: A closed-loop agent built from four decoupled open-source models (VLM observer, LLM summarizer, LLM planner, VLM critic) where the critic checks each action's feasibility on the raw image and triggers replanning.
insight: The critic is the main source of robustness: removing it (CLEA w/o critic) lowers SR by 42.0% relative to full CLEA, because errors such as grasping non-existent objects or opening from closed containers go uncaught. The critic mostly catches outdated (44.4%) and redundant (33.3%) actions, i.e. stale planner assumptions and ignored memory. The authors also report that giving the critic the raw image rather than a text description is crucial, but this is an empirical claim with no ablation shown.
method: Observer: a VLM converts each RGB image plus task info into a structured textual description of task-relevant objects and spatial relations (o_i -> o_i^t).
Memory: a FIFO history buffer of (observation, action, feedback) tuples, plus an LLM summarizer that compresses history into a textual belief state b_i.
Planner: a CoT LLM that takes the belief and observation and outputs a sub-goal and a short action sequence, chosen from a skill pool of Python functions (open, close, pick_from, release_to, go_to).

Critic: a CoT VLM that sees the original image, the belief and the next action before execution, and outputs a validity flag p_i and feedback f_i; if false, the planner replans the sub-goal and actions.
Multi-robot control: one agent controls a mobile dual-arm RM65-B and a stationary Kinova Gen3 arm, with RRT-Connect/MoveIt motion planning and YOLOv11 perception.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (summarizer, planner) and Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct (observer, critic), frozen
setting.observation: RGB images (JPEG) from onboard/depth cameras on two robots, converted to text by a VLM
setting.action_space: predefined skill-pool function calls (open, close, pick_from, release_to, go_to) mapped to low-level operations

numbers_note: Main results are only in a bar-chart figure (SR and Average Score over 12 real-world trials); the text gives only average improvements, not per-task values, so no table numbers are extracted.
results: Over 12 real-world kitchen trials, CLEA beats the open-loop VLM baseline (Yang et al. 2024) by 67.3% in SR and by 52.8% (abstract) or 53.8% (text) in score, and beats CLEA w/o critic by 42.0% SR and 26.3% score. The baseline consistently fails the integration tasks.
limitations: Very small evaluation: 12 real-world trials in a single kitchen, with results shown only in figures and no standard benchmark.
The predefined skill API limits recovery: invalid actions were the most frequent problem (9, 45%), and the critic itself sometimes fails because of VLM perception limits.
LLMs mis-assign actions between the two robots, and running four 72B models is inefficient.
builds_on: Yang et al. 2024 (LLM+VLM task planning with refinement)
compares_to: Open-loop VLM planning baseline (Yang et al. 2024)
